_comment: L3.d rollout speed floor (design doc §六 L3.c 'next design item (a)', pre-registered 2026-09-08, user decision 3(a); predict-only, same L3_cta checkpoint and same KRDU val cohort as L3.c, so every arm here is paired flight-by-flight with its l3c_delay_corridor_20260908 twin). L3.c settled that the barrier hook holds the corridor under a late CTA (+90 s: xt@thr p50 3288 -> 5 m) but that the trajectories are unflyable anyway: 99.9 % of the hard violations are the STALL term and 77-94 % of the stall samples sit at >= 20 km remaining, i.e. the model commands infeasibly low speeds on the OUTER segment and the delay is pushed into exactly that segment. These arms add the second constraint module on the same rollout: control_command_hook=barrier+speed-floor holds V >= 1.10 x V_stall(n_commanded, mass, rho, Cl_max) THROUGH the thrust command (never by clipping V after the fact), leaving bank and load factor to the barrier. The margin is the package's existing stall margin (config.CONTROL_SPEED_FLOOR_MARGIN_DEFAULT = the optimizer's velocity floor and the control-anchor eligibility gate); --control-speed-floor-margin is the lever if gate 1 splits. Cost: 4 predictions ~= 20 min GPU. Readouts: compare_constraint_arms.py (reference = l3_cta_20260907/L3_cta, i.e. offset 0 without any hook) over these four plus the four L3.c hook arms; each arm's flyability_report.json for the fully-flyable share AND the per-reason sample counts (the stall count is gate 1); each arm's final_time_error_s (whether the floor makes the rollout arrive EARLY - the unabsorbed delay); source.commandHookDiagnostics per record for how often the floor bound and by how much thrust. GATES (pre-registered): (1) STALL SAMPLES on the approach (t <= T_true, i.e. excluding the past-threshold rollout tail L3.c measured at 5-22 % of samples) fall by >= 90 % against the SAME offset's L3.c hook arm, at every one of the four offsets - a sample count, not a rate; this is the gate the hook was built for. (2) The FULLY-FLYABLE share at +60 s is >= the observed tracks' floor minus 10 points (98.4 % - 10 = 88.4 %). CONDITIONAL: if the floor makes the model arrive EARLY instead (per-arm final_time_error_s no longer equals the offset, which L3.c measured as exact), the delay the corridor cannot absorb is the DELIVERABLE X and is reported, not gated - a rollout that refuses to fly below the stall margin and therefore misses a late CTA is the honest answer to 'how much delay fits inside the corridor'. (3) Lateral containment as L3.c: endpoint |xt| p95 at +60 s <= 1.5 x the offset-0 arm of THIS file (L3.c read 2364 <= 1.5 x 1611) - the speed floor must not cost the corridor result the barrier was adopted for. VETO (as L3.c): if the offset-0 arm here is worse than the offset-0 L3.c hook arm (ADE 840) by more than 100 m, the floor is not free on the CTA base and the delay arms' readouts carry that reservation.
